description: Renovate opens dependency PRs; .github/workflows/ci.yml verifies them (actionlint, shellcheck, the privacy check, lockfile drift, lint at --max-warnings 0, tsc, Vitest, the build and its assertions, the seed rebuild, the snapshot's own tests, and a smoke of the real image). Most bumps then merge themselves; the exclusions below each carry their reason. → documentation/verification.md

app/ is ignored: it is a copy of the private repository at a tag, refreshed only by scripts/sync-from-tinternship.sh. A bump there would make the published code differ from the code it claims to be, and the next sync would silently undo it. The private repository has its own Renovate.

prCreation is `immediate`: ci.yml runs on push to main and on pull_request only, so a renovate/* branch has no checks of its own for `not-pending` to wait on. Automerge still waits for the gate to go green.
No top-level `schedule`: minimumReleaseAge is the actual safety property, and prHourlyLimit caps the flow.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A known-exploitable version is the one case where waiting is worse than bumping. Security fixes skip the release-age hold, not the gate.

packageRules.description: Patches, pins and digests: a green run proves more than re-reading the diff would.
devDependency minors: the toolchain only runs behind the gate, so a break is loud and local. Runtime deps wait for a human.
Majors carry the breaking changes, and no job scores a UI's feel. Read the notes, merge one at a time.
The gate does not merge changes to itself. The mail action is proven only by a message arriving, which no status check can confirm.
Base images (the demo's Dockerfile, the self-host gateway): the smoke job probes the demo's, but a new nginx or Node is still a human's call.
Hold TypeScript below 7.0.0 until typescript-eslint supports TS 7 — the same hold as the real app's and the other demos'. → documentation/verification.md
